common_name: Telegraph Cucumber (Victorian English Long Greenhouse Cucumber)

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost, or start indoors for an earlier crop; provide a sturdy trellis so the long fruit hangs straight, since fruit that rests on the ground tends to curl.

directions: Sow seed an inch deep in warm, fertile, well-drained soil, then train vines up a trellis for the straightest fruit and easiest picking. Telegraph is a Victorian-era English heirloom, originally bred for greenhouse culture, that produces long, slender, dark green fruit twelve to eighteen inches at full size, with thin, tender, nearly seedless flesh and a mild, sweet, non-bitter flavor prized for slicing. It performs well outdoors in warm climates given a trellis and consistent moisture, though fruit is best picked at eight to twelve inches for the crispest texture, since fully mature fruit can turn coarse. Keep watering even throughout fruit development, since irregular moisture is the most common cause of bitterness and misshapen fruit in this and most cucumber varieties.
